essay.title: SECTION B - THEORY
essay.instruction: Answer four (4) questions. Write your answers clearly and show all necessary workings.

questions.question:
Study the apparatus shown in the diagram below.
(a) Name the process demonstrated by the setup.
(b) Explain the process using the kinetic theory of matter.
(c) State three factors that affect the rate of the process.
(d) Give two everyday examples of the process.

(a) State Boyle's law.
(b) A gas occupies 600 cm³ at a pressure of 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa. Calculate its volume when the pressure is increased to 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa at constant temperature.
(c) State two conditions necessary for Boyle's law to apply.

(a) State Charles' law.
(b) A gas occupies 240 cm³ at 300 K. Calculate its volume at 350 K if the pressure remains constant.
(c) Explain why temperature used in gas-law calculations must be expressed on the Kelvin scale.

(a) Define isotopes.
(b) State two similarities and two differences between isotopes of the same element.
(c) An atom contains 17 protons and 18 neutrons. State its:
(i) Atomic number
(ii) Mass number
(iii) Number of electrons when neutral
(iv) Nuclide representation.

(a) Explain the terms:
(i) Ionic bond
(ii) Covalent bond
(iii) Dative covalent bond
(iv) Hydrogen bond.
(b) State the type of bonding involved in the formation of NH₄⁺ from NH₃ and H⁺.
(c) Explain why water has a relatively high boiling point.

(a) Calculate the relative molecular mass of each of the following:
(i) NH₄Cl
(ii) CaCO₃
(iii) H₂SO₄.
[N = 14, H = 1, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, S = 32]
(b) Calculate the number of moles contained in 25 g of CaCO₃.
